area: A. chart-api (backend chart pipeline: line-chart gateway, chart aggregation, price-tick relay)

files_changed.summary: Rewritten around one continuous wall-clock `all` stream (C1). The 1 Hz boundary closer (self-rescheduling setTimeout aligned to the second; runs from module init, independent of battle lifecycle and of the 2 s leader-load interval) now closes and EMITS exactly one `all` candle every second (flat when idle, battle_id = active battle or null between battles). New leader bootstrap `restoreAllStreamAsLeader` restores the stream from Redis zset `chart:history:all` (+ persisted active candle if fresh, + seed close from latest price_ticks row) so the stream ticks even after a restart during cooldown; resumes from 'now' (no gap-emit burst). `all` history persisted to Redis zset `chart:history:all` (score = bucket ms, member JSON incl. battle_id), trimmed to 900, TTL 24 h, in-memory mirror capped 900. `candleBatch` (all scope) = contiguous last 600 closed seconds + in-progress bucket flagged `partial:true`, `active_battle_id`, `included_battle_ids` (distinct non-null ids actually present), `window_seconds:600`, `server_time` ms, `replace:true`; memoised per wall-clock second (one build shared by every socket); emitted on connection, on `subscribe {reason:'resync'}` (1 s per-socket dedupe) and — legacy compatibility — on a reason-less subscribe only if no batch was sent to that socket in the last 5 s (never two batches per connect). `broadcastCandleBatchOnNewBattle(battleId?)` no longer broadcasts anything; it records the active battle (new `noteBattleStarted`). Late ticks whose bucket was already closed fold into the open bucket instead of being dropped (no notional loss at the boundary). Next bucket opens at the last traded price (fixes a stale seed price when a tick beat the timer). Stragglers of an ended battle (tracked via `lastEndedBattleId`) add volume to `all` but never re-adopt the battle or resurrect its per-battle key. Per-battle keys/archive kept for admin: trim MAX_POINTS 400, live keys `chart:history:battle_<id>` get 24 h TTL on every write (single MULTI: zadd+trim+expire), completed archive `chart:history:completed:<id>` gets 7-day TTL. DB rebuild uses `price_ticks.tradeAmount` as $ volume. `server_time` on candleClosed is now epoch ms. New getters `getLiveAllCandleSnapshot()` (bucket_ts/volume/close/count) and `getActiveBattleId()`. Battle-scope `subscribe {battleId}` now returns that battle's closed candles. Dropped the unused RedisCandleHistoryService dependency (the `ticktrade:candle:history` list is no longer written).

MAX_POINTS 200 -> 400 (per-battle, >= 300 s battle length); new ALL_STREAM_MAX_POINTS=900, CANDLE_BATCH_WINDOW_SECONDS=600, COMPLETED_HISTORY_TTL_SEC (7 d), LIVE_HISTORY_TTL_SEC (24 h); new `AllStreamCandle` (Candle + battle_id: number|null); UnifiedCandlePayload: battle_id may be null, `partial?: boolean`, server_time documented as ms.

Pure helpers for the C1 stream: `resolveTickBucketStart` (late-tick folding), `buildContiguousWindow` (1/s window with flat gap fill, no synthetic leading history), `buildFlatAllStreamCandle`, `collectBattleIds`, `rebuildCandlesFromPriceTicks` (volume = SUM(tradeAmount), count = trades), `priceTickDedupeKey` (eventId first, legacy tuple fallback). `toUnifiedCandle` preserves an explicit `battle_id: null` and sets `partial`. Bug fix: `createCandleState`/`applyTickToState` guard non-finite volume (Math.max(0, NaN) was NaN and poisoned the bucket).

Price-tick section only: handler accepts `eventId`; dedupe via `priceTickDedupeKey` (eventId preferred); heartbeat/unchanged ticks are still dropped when the price equals the last processed price, but a heartbeat carrying a price not yet seen now flows through as a zero-volume tick (so the last price of a coalesced burst reaches the chart); `priceUpdate` gains `bucket_ts` (epoch s of the in-progress `all` bucket) and `volume` ($ accumulated so far) read from `lineChartGateway.getLiveAllCandleSnapshot()`. Existing fields unchanged.

New jest spec (18 tests): volume accumulation incl. NaN/negative guard, late-tick folding, contiguous window/flat fill/window bounds/dedupe/invalid candles, included ids, unified payload contract (seconds, null battle_id, partial, ms server_time), DB rebuild from tradeAmount, eventId dedupe key.

New jest spec (6 tests) driving the gateway with fakes + fake clock: one candle per second incl. flat cooldown seconds with battle_id null and ms server_time; late tick folded (total notional preserved); next bucket opens at last traded price when a tick beat the timer; straggler of ended battle not re-adopted; candleBatch shape (window, partial last, replace, included ids, active id), per-second memo, emit-on-connect only, resync dedupe, legacy 5 s suppression; priceUpdate enrichment getter.

behaviour_changes: `candleClosed` on room `line_chart_all` is now emitted EVERY second, including flat candles (o=h=l=c=last close, volume 0, count 0) and cooldown/idle seconds (battle_id: null); previously only seconds with trades were emitted and nothing was emitted between battles.

`candleBatch` (all scope) now carries the last 600 seconds of the continuous stream plus the in-progress bucket (`partial: true`) with `replace: true`, `window_seconds`, `included_battle_ids` (real), `active_battle_id`, `server_time` in ms — instead of the last 3 COMPLETED battles capped at 200 points (the active battle was never included).

No `candleBatch` broadcast on battle.started any more (clients keep appending the continuous stream). Batch is sent on connection, on `subscribe {scope:'all', reason:'resync'}` (>=1 s apart per socket), and for a reason-less subscribe only if no batch was sent to that socket in the last 5 s (legacy client compatibility; never two batches per connect).
`server_time` on `candleClosed` payloads (all and per-battle rooms) is now epoch milliseconds (was seconds).
`priceUpdate` (main namespace) gains `bucket_ts` and `volume`; all existing fields unchanged.
Price-tick dedupe uses the engine `eventId` when present; heartbeat ticks whose price differs from the last processed price are no longer dropped (zero volume, emitted as priceUpdate/candle price).
Late price ticks for an already-closed second are folded into the open bucket (previously dropped with their volume).
`all` stream history persisted to Redis zset `chart:history:all` (900 points, TTL 24 h); the old list `ticktrade:candle:history` is no longer written.
Per-battle history trim raised 200 -> 400 candles; `chart:history:battle_<id>` keys get a 24 h TTL; `chart:history:completed:<id>` get a 7-day TTL after archive (were immortal).
DB history rebuild (per-battle fallback) uses price_ticks.tradeAmount ($ notional) instead of tick count.
Battle-scope `subscribe {battleId}` returns that battle's own closed candles (previously the completed-battles list).
After a leader restart the `all` stream self-starts (restored from Redis, or seeded from the last price tick) instead of waiting for the first engine tick.
new_settings_env: None added. Existing `DISABLE_WS_GATEWAY_TIMERS` (worker processes) still disables the closer/restore timers. Constants (not env): CANDLE_BATCH_WINDOW_SECONDS=600, ALL_STREAM_MAX_POINTS=900, MAX_POINTS=400 (per battle), LIVE_HISTORY_TTL_SEC=86400, COMPLETED_HISTORY_TTL_SEC=604800, RESYNC_BATCH_DEDUPE_MS=1000, LEGACY_SUBSCRIBE_BATCH_SUPPRESS_MS=5000, ACTIVE_BATTLE_DB_CACHE_MS=5000.

requests_for_other_agents.change: Pass the battle id so the chart marks the round without a DB lookup: replace `void this.lineChartGateway.broadcastCandleBatchOnNewBattle().catch((err) => {` with `void this.lineChartGateway.broadcastCandleBatchOnNewBattle(payload.battleId).catch((err) => {` (method still works without the argument via a cached DB lookup; it no longer broadcasts a batch).

Stamp a unique id on every price tick so the API dedupe is exact (C1): add `eventId: randomUUID(),` (import { randomUUID } from 'node:crypto') to the published `engine:events:price.tick` payload. The API already prefers `payload.eventId` and falls back to battle+ms+price+source when absent. Also note: the API now lets a `source:'heartbeat'` tick through when its price differs from the last processed price for that battle (zero volume), so the once-per-second heartbeat re-publish in the plan will reach the chart; identical-price heartbeats remain no-ops.

Server contract as implemented: on `candleBatch` with `payload.replace === true` replace the store with `payload.candles` (ascending, contiguous 1/s; last element may have `partial: true` — treat it as the in-progress bar, not history). `candleClosed` arrives every second on `line_chart_all` with `battle_id` possibly null and `server_time` in ms (use for the EMA server offset). `priceUpdate` now has `bucket_ts` (epoch s) and `volume` ($ so far in that bucket) — move the in-progress bar only when `bucket_ts` >= last closed timestamp. Do NOT emit `subscribe` on connect (server emits the batch on connection); for foreground/stale resync emit `lineChartSocket.emit('subscribe', { scope: 'all', reason: 'resync' })` (server dedupes to 1/s per socket). `included_battle_ids` now reflects the ids actually in `candles`; `battle_cursor`/`has_more*` are always null/false (legacy).

Optional cleanup: the gateway no longer injects RedisCandleHistoryService and the `ticktrade:candle:history` list has no readers; the service and its registration in redis.module.ts can be deleted (not required for correctness).

The `ticktrade:candle:active` Redis key is written by both the API gateway and the engine's own RedisStateService with the same key name (pre-existing collision, engine file not mine). My restore path guards against it by only accepting a persisted active candle that is fresh (current or previous second) and newer than the last closed bucket; a proper fix is to namespace one of the writers.
notes_for_pdf:
WHAT WAS WRONG

The trading chart had no single source of truth. The backend (apps/api/src/ws/line-chart.gateway.ts) aggregated engine price ticks into 1-second candles, but (1) it only emitted candleClosed for seconds that contained a trade and emitted nothing at all between rounds, while it silently stored flat candles for quiet seconds — so a device that stayed connected saw a different bar density than a device that reconnected; (2) the candleBatch sent on connect contained only the last three COMPLETED battles, capped at 200 points in total, and never the active round, so every sign-in or phone resume drew a vertical "spike" from an hours-old close to the live price; (3) the batch was rebuilt per socket and twice per connect (connection + client subscribe), each build scanning Redis and, on a miss, up to 10 000 price_ticks rows (audit api-ws-perf F11); (4) volume was lossy: the API deduped ticks by (battle, ms, price) which collapsed two trades in the same millisecond, ticks that arrived a few ms after the second boundary were dropped together with their notional, and the DB rebuild path counted ticks instead of dollars so history bars (1–3) sat next to live bars (10 000+); (5) the completed-battle archive keys never expired; (6) the per-battle trim of 200 cut the first 100 s of every 300 s round; (7) after an API restart during cooldown no candle closed until the first engine tick, because the boundary closer only works on keys that already have a live state and last close.

How the boundary closer is driven: it is a self-rescheduling setTimeout aligned to the wall-clock second (scheduleBoundaryClose), started in onModuleInit and independent of the 2 s leader-load interval and of battle lifecycle. It did tick every second already, but produced nothing when the `all` key had no state or no last close, and never emitted flat candles.

WHAT CHANGED

1. One continuous `all` stream (contract C1). The closer now guarantees exactly one closed candle per second on room line_chart_all: a real OHLC/volume candle when trades happened, otherwise a flat candle (o=h=l=c=last close, volume 0, count 0). battle_id is the battle whose trades landed in that second, the active battle for a flat second inside a round, or null for cooldown/idle seconds. Every payload carries server_time in epoch milliseconds. The stream is self-sustaining: ensureAllStreamLive opens the next bucket at the last traded price each second, and restoreAllStreamAsLeader restores state after a restart from the new Redis zset chart:history:all (900 points, TTL 24 h), the persisted active candle when it is fresh, or the latest price_ticks row as a seed — so flat candles keep flowing even if the process restarts during cooldown. A long downtime is not replayed candle by candle (no emit burst); the live stream resumes from "now" and the batch builder fills the visible window with flat candles.

2. candleBatch = last 600 seconds + partial. buildAllCandleBatchPayload returns the last CANDLE_BATCH_WINDOW_SECONDS=600 closed seconds of the stream, contiguous (buildContiguousWindow fills interior/trailing gaps), plus the in-progress bucket as the last element flagged partial:true, with active_battle_id, included_battle_ids computed from the candles actually sent, window_seconds, server_time (ms) and replace:true. It is memoised per wall-clock second (getAllCandleBatchPayload), so a reconnect wave costs one build. It is emitted on connection and on `subscribe {scope:'all', reason:'resync'}` (max once per second per socket). A reason-less subscribe (what pre-C1 clients send right after connect and on every round switch) only gets a batch if none was sent to that socket in the last 5 s, so the new server never sends two batches per connect yet still works with the old client until the PWA is redeployed. Nothing is broadcast on battle.started any more; broadcastCandleBatchOnNewBattle(battleId?) only records the active round (noteBattleStarted).

3. Volume correctness. resolveTickBucketStart folds a tick whose second was already closed into the open bucket instead of dropping it, so traded notional is never lost at the boundary (this also matters for the engine's new trailing coalescer flush). The subscriber (apps/api/src/redis/redis.subscriber.ts, price-tick section only) dedupes by the engine eventId when present (fallback: the old tuple) and no longer drops a heartbeat that carries a price it has not seen (it becomes a zero-volume tick), while identical-price heartbeats stay silent. The DB rebuild (rebuildCandlesFromPriceTicks) sums price_ticks.tradeAmount and counts only trade rows. A spec also caught that Math.max(0, NaN) is NaN, i.e. one non-finite volumeScale would have poisoned a whole bucket; both aggregation helpers now guard it.

4. priceUpdate enrichment. The relay attaches bucket_ts (epoch seconds of the in-progress bucket) and volume ($ accumulated so far) read from a cheap in-memory getter (getLiveAllCandleSnapshot); all existing fields are unchanged. The client uses these only to move the in-progress bar.

5. Housekeeping. Per-battle trim MAX_POINTS 200→400 (≥ the 300 s round), live per-battle zsets get a 24 h TTL on every write (one MULTI: zadd, trim, expire), completed archives get a 7-day TTL, the `all` stream is capped at 900 in memory and Redis. A late tick for a battle that already ended still counts towards `all` but can no longer re-adopt that battle as active or resurrect its per-battle key.

WHY IT IS SAFE

No money math is touched; this is the read-side chart projection. Volume can only go up relative to before (nothing is dropped any more) and every number is still the sum of the engine's volumeScale (trade notional). All per-battle keys, the completed archive and the admin indicator path are kept. Leader gating is unchanged (single broadcaster/candle writer). Payloads are backward compatible: legacy fields (cursor, has_more, battle_cursor, battle_id) are still present, and the 5 s legacy-subscribe rule keeps an old client working. Redis writes per second are unchanged in count (one pipelined MULTI per stream).

HOW TO TEST

Unit: cd apps/api && npx jest src/chart/candle-aggregation.spec.ts src/ws/line-chart.gateway.spec.ts (24 tests; the whole api suite is 78/78). The gateway spec drives closeCandlesAtBoundary under a fake clock and asserts one candle per second through battle end and cooldown with battle_id null, late-tick folding with total notional preserved, correct next-bucket open price, no re-adoption of an ended battle, the batch shape (600-window, partial last, replace, included ids), per-second memoisation, emit-on-connect only, resync dedupe and the legacy 5 s suppression. Build: pnpm --filter api build. Runtime, after the stack is restarted on the new build: connect a socket.io client to /line-chart and confirm one candleBatch on connect (candles ascending, contiguous 1/s, last element partial:true, replace:true, server_time in ms), then a candleClosed every second including during cooldown (battle_id null, volume 0); emit subscribe {scope:'all', reason:'resync'} and confirm exactly one fresh batch; on the main namespace confirm priceUpdate carries bucket_ts and volume; in Redis check `ZCARD chart:history:all` grows to 900 and `TTL chart:history:completed:<id>` is about 604800 after a round ends. To verify volume, sum candle.volume over a round and compare with SUM(tradeAmount) of price_ticks for that battle. Deployment note: deploy the API and PWA builds together; an old client keeps working through the legacy rule, but a new client against an old server would never receive replace:true batches.
